title: Two-condition response over time and individual variability
question: How does the response change over time under two conditions, and how much variation occurs within each?
created_by: A one-time Codex background subagent inspecting the local BioFigure gallery; the user supplied no source case IDs.

queries: 重复测量 时间 轨迹

sources.inspected_finding: A longitudinal panel connects observations with the same UID and overlays a heavier aggregate trend.
sources.transfer: Separate the group trend from the trajectories. Only connect verified individual visits. In the independent design remove the individual line layer.

sources.inspected_finding: R11 computes group-by-time means separately from its raw observations and draws group-specific mean points and lines.
sources.transfer: Compute an arithmetic mean for each condition and observed visit, then overlay both mean trajectories on the same scale. Keep the actual visit times.

sources.inspected_finding: R6 juxtaposes individual observations with a compact quartile summary in order to show their distribution.
sources.transfer: Keep every observation and annotate each visit with a thick 25th–75th percentile bar. Omit density smoothing and separate conditions in facets.

applies_when: Two conditions, a continuous finite quantitative response, explicitly numeric times, and at least two observed times.
One observation per independent individual, or one observation per subject and visit using stable individual IDs. The design must state which strategy applies.
Goal is descriptive comparison with no modeled trend or significance claim.
reject_when: Unknown sampling design, missing subject IDs, non-unique observation IDs, duplicate individual/visit rows, or subject IDs shared between conditions.
Independent design contains repeated subjects, or repeated design has no returning subjects.
Data are group means only or contain unaggregated technical replicates; inference or adjustment for confounding is the principal goal.
actions: Use a common quantitative time scale and common response limits. Style condition means with redundant color, shape and line type.
Keep individual points and within-cell interquartile bars below. Draw same-subject segments only between adjacent scheduled visits when sampling is repeated.
Compute n, arithmetic means and type-7 quartiles from plotted rows; export exact source and target observation IDs from the same segment table used for drawing.
limitations: Two-group template. Equal observations can overplot; large cohorts, many visits, irregular continuous collection or long labels need separate usability validation.
IQR describes observed spread, not uncertainty. This method supplies no mixed model, treatment contrast, or causal inference. A single observation cannot show a spread.
With no planned_times the method infers visit order from observed times. Missing visits absent from both conditions cannot then be identified.
Visual interpretation of gallery examples used original PNGs and R code. R6/R11 share one source family, so three gallery records represent two source families.
Learning input is simulated. No real-user preference, independent user acceptance, production gate or model training is implied. English or Latin axis labels are covered by the preview PDF device.

style_option.effect: Larger raw points and lower individual-line opacity. Group summaries, time coordinates and edge connectivity are unchanged.
